'''Francis Stanley "Frank" Kaminsky III'''<ref>{{cite web|url=http://espn.go.com/espn/feature/story/_/id/11822147/wisconsin-badgers-big-man-frank-kaminsky-back-senior-season|title=Wisconsin Badgers big man Frank Kaminsky is back for senior season|work=ESPN.com}}</ref> (born April 4, 1993) is an American [[Power forward (basketball)|power forward]] basketball player who recently completed his college career for the [[Wisconsin Badgers men's basketball|Wisconsin Badgers]]. Kaminsky attended [[Benet Academy]] in [[Lisle, Illinois]]. He currently holds the Wisconsin single game record for points (43).<ref>{{cite news|title=Wisconsin's Frank Kaminsky nets school record 43 points in rout|url=http://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/2013/11/19/wisconsin-frank-kaminsky-school-record-43-points-north-dakota/3647683/|publisher=Associated Press|accessdate=19 November 2013|date=November 19, 2013}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Three and change|url=http://espn.go.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/10172331/wisconsin-badgers-frank-kaminsky-thank-scoring-success-espn-magazine|publisher=ESPN|accessdate=26 December 2013}}</ref> He was the unanimous men's [[List of U.S. men's college basketball national player of the year awards|National College Player of the Year]] in 2015.

==Early life and high school career==
Kaminsky's father, Frank, played basketball at Lewis University. His mother, Mary, played volleyball at Northwestern.<ref>[http://www.uwbadgers.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/frank_kaminsky_761576.html "Frank Kaminsky Bio"]. uwbadgers.com. Retrieved April 5, 2015.</ref> In 1998, when he was 5 years old, his aunt and uncle worked for the [[Chicago Bulls]] and he had access to the practice facility when [[Michael Jordan]], [[Dennis Rodman]] and [[Randy Brown]] were there.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://espn.go.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/10866360/frank-kaminsky-wisconsin-badgers-says-nba-looks-boring|title=Frank Kaminsky: Badgers to be great|accessdate=2014-05-01|date=2014-05-01|publisher=[[ESPN]]}}</ref>

Kaminsky attended [[Benet Academy]] in [[Lisle, Illinois]]. He was named first-team all-state by the [[Chicago Sun-Times]] and IBCA and second-team all-state by the [[Associated Press|AP]] after averaging 14.2 points, 8.7 rebounds, 4.2 blocks and 2.8 assists during his senior season. He led the Redwings to a 29-1 season after being defeated in the Sectional Semifinals by the East Aurora Tomcats that were led by Connecticut Huskies superstar and National Champion Ryan Boatright. He was also named all-area, all-conference and [[East Suburban Catholic Conference]] Player of the Year.

==College career==

===Freshman season===
Kaminsky played in 35 of 36 games as a freshman. He scored a season-high nine points against [[UMKC Kangaroos men's basketball|UMKC]] on November 22, 2011.

===Sophomore season===
Kaminsky played in 32 games, starting the first two games of the season. He finished the season averaging 4.2 points and 1.8 rebounds per game. He led the team in free-throw percentage at 76.7%. He posted a season-high 19 points at [[Illinois Fighting Illini men's basketball|Illinois]] on February 3, 2013.

===Junior season===
On November 19, 2013, Kaminsky broke the Wisconsin single game scoring record with 43 points against [[University of North Dakota men's basketball|North Dakota]].<ref>{{cite web|title=School Record 43 points from Frank Kaminsky power UW past North Dakota|url=http://host.madison.com/sports/college/basketball/men/badgers-men-s-basketball-school-record-points-from-frank-kaminsky/article_f05e4e99-486c-5332-bdbb-77b253f436a0.html|publisher=Madison.com|accessdate=26 December 2013}}</ref> Kaminsky shot 16 of 19 from the field, including six of six from 3-point range and five of six from the free throw line. The previous Wisconsin single game record was 42 points set by Ken Barnes (vs. [[Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball|Indiana]] on March 8, 1965) and [[Michael Finley]] (vs. [[Eastern Michigan Eagles men's basketball|Eastern Michigan]] on December 10, 1994).

At the conclusion of the regular season, Kaminsky was named to the First Team All-Big Ten.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.bigten.org/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/031014aag.html|title=Big Ten Announces 2014 Men's Basketball Postseason Honors: Michigan's Stauskas named Big Ten Player of the Year|accessdate=2014-03-10|date=2014-03-10|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|work=BigTen.org}}</ref>

On March 29, 2014, Kaminsky scored 28 points and had 11 rebounds as Wisconsin defeated #1 seeded [[2013–14 Arizona Wildcats men's basketball team|Arizona]] 64–63 in overtime during the [[2014 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|NCAA Tournament]] to advance to the Final Four. After the game, Kaminsky was named West Regional Most Outstanding Player.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/-college-basketball-mens-tournament/news/20140402/frank-kaminsky-bo-ryan-wisconsin-final-four/|title=Frank Kaminsky Jr. finally finds his moment|accessdate=2014-04-03|date=2014-04-02|publisher=[[Sports Illustrated]]|work=SI.com}}{{deadlink|date=April 2015}}</ref>

===Senior season===
Ahead of the 2014 season Kaminsky was named the Big Ten preseason player of the year.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.jsonline.com/blogs/sports/279414882.html|title=Frank Kaminsky named Big Ten preseason player of the year|author=Jeff Potrykus|work=jsonline.com}}</ref> The Badgers were unanimously picked to win the Big Ten Championship.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.foxsports.com/wisconsin/story/badgers-unanimous-pick-to-win-big-ten-basketball-title-101614|title=Wisconsin Badgers unanimous pick to win Big Ten basketball title|author=Fox Sports|work=FOX Sports}}</ref> The Badgers ended up winning both the Big Ten regular season and the Big Ten tournament.

Kaminsky was named [[2015 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|consensus first-team All-American]].<ref>http://www.uwbadgers.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/033015aac.html</ref> On March 31, 2015 he was named the [[NABC Player of the Year|National Association of Basketball Coaches Player of the Year]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.bigten.org/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/033115aaa.html|title=Kaminsky Named NABC POY Big Ten Conference Official Site|work=bigten.org}}</ref> On April 3 he was named [[Associated Press College Basketball Player of the Year]], the first Wisconsin player to receive the award since its creation in 1961.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.indystar.com/story/sports/2015/04/03/wisconsins-frank-kaminsky-chosen-ap-player-year/25247945/|title=Wisconsin's Frank Kaminsky chosen AP Player of the Year|author=Associated Press, @ap|date=3 April 2015|work=Indianapolis Star}}</ref> He also received the [[Oscar Robertson Trophy]] as the United States Basketball Writers Association College Player of the Year.<ref>http://bleacherreport.com/articles/2419025-frank-kaminsky-wins-2015-oscar-robertson-mens-college-player-of-the-year-award</ref> On April 5, he was named the [[Naismith College Player of the Year]].<ref>http://bleacherreport.com/articles/2420039-frank-kaminsky-named-2015-naismith-mens-college-player-of-the-year</ref> On April 10, he won both the [[John R. Wooden Award]] and [[Kareem Abdul-Jabbar Center of the Year Award]].<ref>http://www.foxsports.com/college-basketball/story/wisconsin-badgers-frank-kaminsky-wins-center-of-the-year-041015</ref> On June 12th Kaminsky was named University of Wisconsin's Male Athlete of the Year.<ref>http://www.uwbadgers.com/genrel/061215aab.html</ref>
